# WO-508: Runner: do not log the same "escalation waiting" note every day
Status: queued (pre-approved: start when a WIP slot frees, see Order; note it on GROK_BOARD.md first)
Vendor: grok
Agent: backend-core (Derek Olsen)

## Goal
When the next rung is held (a letter still awaits approval, a manual letter is open, or the legal window is open), `_escalate` logs an `escalation_waiting` Event on every scheduled run (`engine/runner.py:834-849`). A daily job therefore adds an identical row per held broker per day to the audit log, which grows by hundreds of rows a week at 400 brokers and drowns real events in every history read. Log it once per (broker, rung, why) until something changes: before writing, look at that broker's recent events (`store.events(profile.id, broker.id, limit=50)`, `storage/db.py:372`) and skip the write if the newest `escalation_waiting` already has the same `rung`, `why` and `until`. Behaviour of the ladder itself does not change.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Two consecutive runs with the same hold write one `escalation_waiting` Event, not two.
2. A change in `why` (awaiting_approval then legal_window), in `rung` or in `until` writes a new Event.
3. After the held letter is sent and the ladder moves, a later hold of the same kind writes a new Event again (the newest waiting event is older than the last `escalated` event).
4. Dry runs behave the same (`escalation_due` events, `runner.py:850-853`, get the same de-duplication per rung).
5. The event list read is bounded (one call, `limit <= 50`) and costs nothing when no events exist.
6. Escalation outcomes (`escalated`, `escalation_failed`, state changes) are exactly as before; existing runner tests pass unchanged.

**Limits (every Grok WO, CLAUDE-G-004):** offline only. No network, credentials, git or gh, installs, or running the real app against real sites or a real mailbox; never read anything outside the repo. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Tests pass on Windows too (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`). Check `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/`, `tests/grok/` and the in-house `tests/test_*.py` first; don't duplicate a guard.

No contract changes: `models.py`, `interfaces.py`, `state.py`, `registry.py`, `storage/`, `schema/`, `cli.py`, `config.py`, `paths.py`, `netpolicy.py`, `consent.py`, `crypto.py`, `secrets.py`, `secret_backends.py`, `logging_setup.py`, `engine/browser.py`.
